item.question: The congruence of two triangles is written as ΔABC ≅ ΔXYZ. Why does the order of the letters matter? Is ΔACB ≅ ΔXYZ a correct way to write the same fact, and is ΔACB ≅ ΔXZY?
steps: Read ΔABC ≅ ΔXYZ as an instruction: the first letters go together, the second letters go together and the third letters go together. A lands on X, B on Y and C on Z.

Read ΔACB ≅ ΔXYZ the same way. The first letters give A on X. The second letters give C on Y, and the third letters give B on Z. That is a different matching from the real one, so a long side would be laid on a short side.
Read ΔACB ≅ ΔXZY. The first letters give A on X, the second letters give C on Z, and the third letters give B on Y. These are exactly the pairs of the real matching.
The left side was shuffled and the right side was shuffled the same way, so the message did not change.

item.question: What are the main ideas of the chapter, in order?
item.answer: Congruent figures land exactly on each other, and turning or flipping is allowed. steps: Count what is in play first: 25 squares less the blocked middle one leaves 24.
